constraints: solve for the variable with coefficient 1; integer solutions
hints: Rearrange one equation so a variable with coefficient one is alone.
Replace that variable in the other equation and solve the one-variable result.
Back-substitute and verify the ordered pair in both equations.

constraints: distribute a coefficient over the substituted expression
hints: Use the isolated expression wherever x appears in the second equation.
Distribute the outside coefficient across every term of that expression.
Solve for y, recover x, and check both original equations.

constraints: subtraction of substituted expressions; integer solutions
hints: Isolate one variable from either equation before substitution.
Use parentheses when substituting so a preceding subtraction changes every term correctly.
Solve, back-substitute, and check both equations with the pair.

constraints: coefficients already opposite; integer solutions
hints: Add the equations term by term because one variable's coefficients are opposites.
Solve the resulting one-variable equation.
Substitute that value into either original equation to find the other coordinate.

constraints: matching coefficients; subtract carefully
hints: Align like variables in the two equations before combining them.
Subtract one full equation from the other, changing every sign in the subtracted row.
Solve the remaining variable and back-substitute to verify.

constraints: solutions may include negatives; verify in both equations
hints: Add the equations to cancel the variable with opposite coefficients.
Solve the remaining equation even if its value is negative.
Back-substitute and check both original equations rather than only the combined one.

constraints: scale to create opposite coefficients; integer solutions
hints: Multiply one entire equation by a factor that makes one pair of coefficients opposites.
Add the scaled equation to the other and solve the surviving variable.
Use an original equation for back-substitution and verify both coordinates.

constraints: scale both to match one variable; integer solutions
hints: Choose multipliers that give the same magnitude for one variable in both equations.
Scale every term in both equations, then subtract or add to eliminate that variable.
Back-substitute the result and check it in the unscaled equations.

constraints: negative multipliers turn subtraction into addition
hints: Choose a negative multiplier so that adding, rather than subtracting, cancels a variable.
Multiply every term by that negative number before adding rows.
Solve, back-substitute, and verify the pair in the original system.

constraints: elimination ends in a false statement (none) or 0 = 0 (infinite)
hints: Eliminate a variable and inspect the remaining numerical statement.
A false numerical statement signals incompatible equations; an identity signals the same line.
Use that statement to decide whether the system has none or infinitely many solutions.

objective: Detect special cases from slopes and graphs
constraints: parallel -> none; same line -> infinitely many; else one
hints: Put both lines in slope-intercept form to compare direction and vertical position.
Equal slopes with different intercepts never meet; equal slopes with equal intercepts describe one line.
Use the comparison to choose the requested classification fields.

constraints: mix all three cases across generated problems
hints: Compare the coefficients after lining up both equations.
If elimination leaves one variable value, there is one intersection; a false or identity statement gives a special case.
Classify from that algebraic result rather than from appearance.

objective: Check a point against both inequalities
constraints: the point must satisfy BOTH inequalities
hints: Substitute the candidate point into the first inequality and compute its residual.
Do the same for the second inequality.
The point is in the overlap only when both resulting comparisons are true.

objective: Boundary styles and the overlap region
constraints: one strict and one inclusive inequality per problem
hints: Rewrite each boundary in y = mx + c form before describing it.
The inequality with equality uses a solid boundary; the strict inequality uses a dashed boundary.
Use the comparison direction to decide whether each half-plane is above or below its boundary.

objective: Locate a point in the solution region
constraints: candidate points off the boundary lines
hints: Test each candidate in the lower-bound inequality and the upper-bound inequality.
Keep only a point whose y-value is strictly between the two expressions.
Verify it does not land on either boundary line.

constraints: one count equation and one value equation
hints: Let variables count the two pass types, then write one equation for total count.
Write a second equation by multiplying each count by its ticket value and adding.
Solve the pair and check both the number of items and the euro total.

constraints: two purchases of the same two items; elimination-friendly numbers
hints: Assign one variable to each unit price and translate each purchase into an equation.
Eliminate or substitute to isolate one price.
Use the other purchase to check both recovered unit prices.

constraints: verify counts are nonnegative integers and totals match
hints: Write count and value equations for the two ticket types.
Solve for the requested ticket count.
Verify the counts are nonnegative integers and reproduce both stated totals.

objective: Set up the amount and value equations
constraints: amount equation plus concentration (pure-substance) equation
hints: The total-volume equation adds the two ingredient amounts.
For pure substance, multiply each amount by its decimal concentration before adding.
Match total volume and pure amount to the requested four quantities.

constraints: target strength strictly between the two ingredient strengths
hints: Let each variable be litres of one solution, then add them for total volume.
Use decimal concentration times litres for the salt-content equation.
Solve the two equations and check that the amounts add to the required volume.

constraints: blend price between the two ingredient prices; halves allowed
hints: Let each variable be kilograms of one coffee type.
Write one equation for total mass and one for total euro value using price times mass.
Check the two masses add to the blend mass and produce its stated value.

objective: Current and wind: sum and difference
constraints: downstream = sum, upstream = difference of the two rates
hints: With the flow, ground speed combines still speed and flow speed; against it, their difference applies.
Add the two ground-speed equations to recover twice the still speed.
Use either equation to find the flow speed and check both directions.

objective: Compute the two speeds from d = rt first
constraints: distances divide evenly by the times
hints: First use distance divided by time to calculate each ground speed.
Treat those two speeds as with-flow and against-flow rates.
Use their sum and difference to find the two requested speeds.

constraints: meeting problems: combined speed = total distance / time
hints: Divide total separation by meeting time to find the sum of the two speeds.
Pair that sum with the given speed difference as two equations.
Solve for both speeds and check their sum times the time gives the distance.
